study.question: Can the incumbent pooled elapsed-time/recurrence representation be executed and optimized in its compact coordinates without losing its learned function or validation quality? Source inspection of g1-r0019-pooled_observed finds 16 gap-head coordinates (12 measured counts and 4 deterministic products) replicated isometrically into4096 inputs. The source also computes 4x4x256 context tables and four lifted views before selecting a global view. At seed42 the incumbent reaches AUC0.6302753101, Logloss0.1928112951, wall834.09s, throughput117507.62/s, peak828511744 bytes. Those costs include the entire unchanged pre-gap model; removing this branch overhead need not materially speed the system. This question follows observed redundant execution, not an assumption that another fine history partition must improve prediction.
study.hypothesis: Directly histogramming pooled adjacent gaps retains exactly N,C,B by gap and computes the same pooled C*B/N, while avoiding discarded context coordinates. Collapsing256 identical input copies per statistic preserves the gap-head function class, but an ordinary compact parameter A=sum_i(W_i)/16 changes Adam step geometry. A calibrated mean parameter U=mean_i(W_i), evaluated as A=16U with derivative dA/dU=1/16, should preserve each duplicate-column gradient and therefore its Adam moments/epsilon in exact arithmetic under elementwise Adam with zero state, no weight decay and no global parameter-dependent clipping. This is a conditional algebraic claim, not established full-trajectory equivalence. A native A parameter is the discriminating optimization control. No new predictive information or population mechanism is proposed.

study.proposed_difference: Four standalone source modules form sequential controlled replacements: dense_lifted reconstructs the incumbent; direct_lifted changes only the computation of the identical final gap input; direct_calibrated removes256 duplicate columns per input and calibrates only that layer gradient through an explicit detach-based reparameterization; direct_native uses the same compact16->16->1 architecture and initial effective matrix with ordinary A gradients. The head shrinks from65552 to272 parameters, a65280 reduction; expected whole-model count17187843 versus17253123. This is a source-derived count, not a measured cost result. First-layer nominal MACs drop65536->256 per impression, but pre-gap costs and embeddings dominate. The gap head has the same function class on its selected inputs. No statistical novelty/priority claim: authorized paper searches for time intervals and compression/weight tying returned no additional papers, so a comprehensive nearest-work search is unavailable and novelty remains unverified.
predictions: dense_lifted should reproduce the incumbent seed42 result under identical host execution. Establish this anchor before attributing differences to other arms. Runtime diagnostics should show exact direct/dense and independent-oracle raw counts and conservation (tolerance1e-6).

direct_lifted should retain the same lifted input, parameters, initialization and gradients as dense_lifted. Any performance difference is expected to be negligible numerical/runtime variation; reduced wall/GPU/peak memory and end-to-end inference latency would support actual execution savings.

direct_calibrated should match the same-checkpoint projection within relative numerical error and retain validation AUC/Logloss, while reducing registered parameters by65280. Predeclare projection absolute diagnostic alert1e-4; interpret scale and kernels if exceeded. Expected optimization equivalence is conditional on the frozen host recipe having no weight decay/global clipping; it is not assumed from the public protocol alone.

direct_native has identical input information and initial function, but under ordinary Adam its effective first-gap-layer step is about16 times smaller than the lifted or calibrated arm. Native/calibrated differences would support an optimization-geometry explanation, not information preservation or a more expressive model.

Use AUC loss<=0.0001 and Logloss loss<=0.00005 against the rerun dense_lifted as preliminary practical retention screens, not statistical noninferiority claims. Demand at least3% measured end-to-end throughput or wall improvement before describing a practically useful speed gain; parameter savings alone are reported separately.

Pure Python arithmetic checks already passed without torch or data/training execution: replicated projection error1.73e-18; calibrated first-coordinate Adam update error1.04e-17; native effective update differs0.01499999 for a fixed synthetic gradient. Threshold, empty/singleton, tied/missing/padded support and context-summed count identities passed. These verify arithmetic and conventions only, not host PyTorch execution.

On host, diagnostics compare direct counts with inherited tables on512 label-free rows and independent quadratic oracle on<=8; check padding, input reorder, empty length, empty mask, missing brands, tied timestamps, target/action invariance of THIS branch, zero-input residual, and same-checkpoint projection. At most64 finite scalars. These are candidate-supplied checks and remain subject to source scrutiny. Analyze host-provided full-population and existing slices; no new slice effect is a confirmatory claim.
falsifiers: Any direct/dense count or oracle mismatch, lost edge mass, or nonfinite boundary behavior invalidates the proposed faithful execution replacement. Correct the implementation before interpreting AUC; a numerical/code failure is not scientific counterevidence.

A reproducible validation drop in direct_lifted despite matched source-level inputs falsifies practical reproducibility under the current host execution and requires implementation/numerical diagnosis, not a claim that information was lost.

Calibrated/native at equal272 head parameters show a persistent difference after initialization checks and paired seeds: this rejects the view that ordinary compact Adam automatically preserves the expanded parameterization. It does not establish that the chosen gradient calibration is generally useful.

If calibrated compaction loses quality repeatedly despite exact arithmetic checks, reject practical training equivalence for this host recipe; global clipping, decay, mixed precision and floating reduction drift remain alternative explanations until separately controlled.

If full-model latency, wall and peak allocation do not improve measurably, reject an end-to-end efficiency claim even when parameter and local MAC reductions are algebraically correct. If all compact variants retain quality, that supports sufficiency of the retained statistic head, not independence of histories or irrelevance of pre-gap context.
alternative_explanations: One selected seed, shared validation reused for20 rounds, numerical trajectory divergence and checkpoint selection can explain small AUC differences; current observations are preliminary and require paired repetitions.

Host optimizer details beyond publicly declared Adam may break the analytical moment match: nonzero weight decay, global norm clipping, fused/mixed precision or loss-scale handling. No private training internals are inspected and no frozen recipe is silently changed.
Direct pooled counts are exact integers but projection reductions and GPU kernels reorder floating sums. Small per-batch differences may compound across3 epochs.
The unchanged identity/overlap/transition branches may dominate runtime or memory; allocator warmup, kernel scheduling and machine noise can mask a local speed saving.

The compact head reduces stored parameters but has the same effective feature-function class. A native/control quality change can reflect effective Adam step scale rather than regularization, effective predictive capacity or representation information.

Complete-pair/timestamp-singleton filtering excludes events, particularly16.43 tied events per impression in the prior diagnostic sample. This study inherits that limitation; no conclusion transfers to complete raw logs, actual item identities or production point-in-time data.
